title: Rafael and the Garden
premise: Rafael Vasquez, a mercenary sworn to a god that went silent a decade ago, has never left the valley where magic cannot follow — until a dying stranger presses a map into his hands and dies with Rafael's name on his lips. The map leads beneath Mount Cael to the Unseelie court, where Rafael's own soul was sold at birth by a mother desperate to buy rain for a dying valley. With his sharp-tongued partner Marguerite and a last dragon whose fire is guttering out, Rafael must steal his soul back before the court's queen uses it to snuff the final flame and plunge the world into endless winter. He succeeds only by refusing power outright: he shatters his soul rather than let it be wielded, freeing himself from both the court and the silent god, and chooses an ordinary life in the valley as his true belonging.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent twelve years cataloguing medieval herbals before turning to fantasy. She writes in a converted greenhouse in Cornwall, surrounded by plants that stubbornly refuse to die.

chapters.title: The Valley That Magic Forgot
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. We meet him taking a routine contract in the godless valley, where spells fail and mercenaries like him are hired precisely because they're ordinary. A stranger stumbles into the tavern, bleeding light instead of blood, and dies clutching a map that bears Rafael's childhood name. Emotional beat: unease — the past has found him.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She deciphers the map's margins: it names Rafael as 'collateral,' sold before his first breath. She urges burning it; Rafael, haunted by his mother's silence, refuses. They argue bitterly, then she agrees to come anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over reason, friendship tested by secrets.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Crossing the valley's edge, magic floods back — overwhelming, intoxicating, terrifying. Rafael feels his dormant soul stir for the first time and likes it too much. They reach the mountain gate guarded by a dying dragon, Emberlast, who demands a price: carry her final ember to the court and let her see it burn once more. Emotional beat: temptation's first whisper.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Descending through bone-lit tunnels, they pose as soul-brokers to enter the Unseelie court, a glittering place where mortals are currency. Rafael is recognized instantly — the queen smiles at him like family. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder; home should not feel like this.

chapters.title: The Queen of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The queen reveals the truth: his mother traded his soul to end a drought, and the court has nurtured it like a hothouse flower ever since. She offers Rafael a place beside her — power, permanence, belonging. He nearly says yes. Emotional beat: seduction; corruption begins not with evil but with comfort.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. While Rafael lingers at court, Marguerite trades her memories of their partnership to a broker for the location of the soul-vault. She wakes not knowing why she's protecting this stranger, only that she must. Emotional beat: sacrifice made invisible — love that forgets itself.

chapters.title: The Vault of Sold Names
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Guided by Emberlast's ember, Rafael breaks into the vault and finds thousands of bottled souls — including his own, singing his mother's lullaby. As he takes it, alarms of silver sound. Marguerite, memoryless, covers his escape without knowing why. Emotional beat: grief and awe; reclaiming what was given away freely.

chapters.title: What the God Was Doing All Along
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Fleeing upward, Rafael discovers the truth: his silent god never abandoned the valley — it has been holding the mountain shut from within, weakening as the court grows fat on stolen souls. The queen offers one final trade: return the soul, and the god lives; keep it, and everything burns. Emotional beat: the cost of every choice laid bare.

chapters.title: The Last Ember
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the mountain's throat, the queen attacks; Emberlast spends her final fire shielding them, and the god's failing grip shatters. Rafael holds his soul — whole, powerful, his — and understands that keeping it would make him the next queen. He crushes it. The released essence reignites the god, seals the court, and frees the stolen souls. Emotional beat: triumph through renunciation.

chapters.title: Seeds in Ordinary Soil
chapters.summary: Resolution, Marguerite's POV. Her memories return as the freed souls scatter, and she finds Rafael planting a garden over the sealed mountain — Emberlast's ashes feeding the soil. The god speaks once, softly, then rests. Rafael belongs nowhere grand and everywhere small. Emotional beat: quiet peace; identity found not in power but in choice.
